articles.title: AutoShip: Simplifying Cross-Platform E-commerce Listing
articles.excerpt: What I Built During our hackathon journey at InnoHacks, my team and I worked on AutoShip, a solution designed to simplify one of the biggest challenges faced by small and medium-sized e-commerce selle…
articles.body: What I Built During our hackathon journey at InnoHacks, my team and I worked on AutoShip, a solution designed to simplify one of the biggest challenges faced by small and medium-sized e-commerce sellers: listing the same product across multiple online marketplaces. Manually creating product listings on different platforms is repetitive, time-consuming, and prone to errors. Sellers often need to rewrite product titles and descriptions, upload images again, and manage product information separately for every marketplace. That’s where AutoShip comes in! Our goal is to build a bridge between marketplaces like Amazon and eBay, helping sellers simplify their workflow, reduce repetitive tasks, and expand their reach to international customers.

articles.title: How Multica Agents and Claude Code Built a Godot Game
articles.excerpt: Spring Rider is a Powder-style top-down downhill mountain-bike game in Godot 4.5. You ride an endless spring forest, or race 15 rivals down a glacier-to-valley course traced from the real Mégavalanche…
articles.body: Spring Rider is a Powder-style top-down downhill mountain-bike game in Godot 4.5. You ride an endless spring forest, or race 15 rivals down a glacier-to-valley course traced from the real Mégavalanche. I wrote almost none of its code. A team of Multica agents and a Claude Code session in my terminal built it in 13 days, and my job was research, direction, and saying yes or no. This post covers how we worked: the research we did before the code, the free assets and sounds the game runs on, how I put the agent team together, and how the agents kept out of each other's way. ## Research came before the first line of code The game started with a look, not a mechanic. I wanted the top-down view of the skiing game Powder, moved onto a mountain bike in a spring forest.
articles.author: Bojan Tomic

articles.title: The Verify Loop: Every AI Detector Should Ship With a One-Click Fix
articles.excerpt: Most AI detectors are anxiety as a service. They scan your text, flash a scary "98% AI-generated" score, and leave you staring at the screen wondering what to do next. I just shipped an AI detector on…
articles.body: Most AI detectors are anxiety as a service. They scan your text, flash a scary "98% AI-generated" score, and leave you staring at the screen wondering what to do next. I just shipped an AI detector on my free tools site, and I refused to build it that way. Instead I built what I call the verify loop : Detect → Humanize → Verify. Here's why it matters and how it works. The problem with flag-only detectors A detection score without a fix creates exactly one emotion: panic. Students rewrite randomly, professionals paraphrase blindly, and nobody learns what "sounding human" actually means. The tool did its job (detection) and abandoned the user at the worst moment.
articles.author: Shahzaib

articles.title: The Cost Guardrails I Set Up Before GCP Could Surprise Me
articles.excerpt: Solo builders do not have a finance department. I am the finance department. So before I let any real workload touch my GCP project, I spent one evening building billing guardrails. Not because I am f…
articles.body: Solo builders do not have a finance department. I am the finance department. So before I let any real workload touch my GCP project, I spent one evening building billing guardrails. Not because I am frugal for its own sake — because a surprise bill is the fastest way to kill momentum on a side project. Here is what I set up, in the order I did it, and what each layer actually caught. Layer 1: budgets with teeth The first thing I did was create a billing budget in the Cloud Billing console. Not the vague kind — a budget with notification thresholds at 50%, 90%, and 100% of the monthly amount I am willing to spend on the personal project. The part people skip: the 100% alert alone is useless. By the time you hit 100% of a monthly budget, the month is over.
articles.author: Purvansh Bhatt

articles.title: Cloud Run Jobs vs. Cloud Functions for Batch Security Scans: What I Actually Run in Production
articles.excerpt: I run periodic security scans as part of my incident-readiness platform: dependency checks, config drift detection, TLS posture checks against customer-facing assets. All of it is batch work on a sche…
articles.body: I run periodic security scans as part of my incident-readiness platform: dependency checks, config drift detection, TLS posture checks against customer-facing assets. All of it is batch work on a schedule, not request-driven. When I first designed the pipeline, the obvious GCP answer was Cloud Functions — trigger on a Pub/Sub message from Cloud Scheduler, do the scan, write results to a database, done. It worked. It was also the wrong choice, and it took me a month of fighting timeouts and half-finished scans to figure out why. This post is the decision framework I wish I had: when to use Cloud Functions and when to use Cloud Run Jobs for security batch work, with the actual code and configs that run in production today.
articles.author: Purvansh Bhatt

articles.title: X-AgentRed: How Red-Teaming Multi-Service Agent Ecosystems Exposes Compositional Security Failures
articles.excerpt: Personal agents that chain tool calls across Gmail, Slack, Jira, and payment APIs create a new attack surface. A benign user request can produce harmful outcomes when actions accumulate and interact a…
articles.body: Personal agents that chain tool calls across Gmail, Slack, Jira, and payment APIs create a new attack surface. A benign user request can produce harmful outcomes when actions accumulate and interact across service boundaries. X-AgentRed is a red-teaming framework that discovers these compositional failures by building a directed graph of tool dependencies, sampling attack paths, and using execution feedback to refine them. The paper (arXiv 2610.13886v1) addresses the gap between single-tool security testing and the reality of multi-service orchestration. Existing red-teaming methods prompt LLMs to generate harmful scenarios or decompose known attack objectives into benign-looking steps.
articles.author: mech.app

articles.title: Agent37's $0.37/Month Sandbox: What Low-Cost Agent Isolation Reveals About Deployment Economics
articles.excerpt: Agent37 runs AI agent sandboxes for an average of $0.37 per month per customer. That is roughly 10% of what most sandbox providers charge. The YC F26 company launched on Hacker News with a claim that…
articles.body: Agent37 runs AI agent sandboxes for an average of $0.37 per month per customer. That is roughly 10% of what most sandbox providers charge. The YC F26 company launched on Hacker News with a claim that their infrastructure cost for free-tier users averages $0.05 to $0.10 per month. The pricing is not a loss leader. It reflects architectural choices that expose the true cost structure of agent execution environments. The plumbing matters because agent workloads have predictable resource patterns. They spike CPU during initialization and tool calls, then idle. They need RAM for browser automation and computer-use tasks, then release it. Most sandbox providers provision for peak load and bill accordingly. Agent37 provisions for average load and shares resources across tenants.

articles.title: Astronomers witness supermassive black hole gorge on a cosmic meal before 'burping' radio jets 300 days later
articles.excerpt: Using the NASA spacecraft Swift, astronomers observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal.
articles.body: Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies. The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster . The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.title: The 'Halloween Fireballs' are coming. Here's what to expect from the Taurids this year
articles.excerpt: The Southern and Northern Taurid meteor showers will produce occasional bright, slow-moving meteors worldwide during October and November, with moon-free peaks in 2026.
articles.body: They don't produce anything like the torrent of "shooting stars" associated with August's Perseids or December's Geminids, but the Taurid meteor showers have something else going for them — fireballs. The Taurids are famous for occasionally producing exceptionally bright, slow-moving meteors that can streak dramatically across the night sky from September to December. As a bonus, they're visible from both the Northern and Southern hemispheres. That's because they appear to emanate from the constellation Taurus, which sits close to the ecliptic, the apparent path the sun takes across the sky as Earth orbits around it. The Taurids are actually two closely related showers — the Southern Taurids and Northern Taurids — whose activity overlaps in late October and November.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 12, 1964: The Soviet Union launches Voskhod 1, the 1st multi-person cosmonaut crew, into space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight . This was the first time that a spacecraft carried more than one person into orbit, with three cosmonauts packed inside the spacecraft. Only two cosmonauts were originally supposed to fly on this mission, but Soviet politicians pressured the Russian space program to add one more. This left no room for spacesuits on board, so this also became the first spaceflight without spacesuits . Two of the crewmembers, an engineer and a doctor, became the first civilians to go to space. On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched the first multiperson mission, Voskhod 1, which launched three Russian cosmonauts into space.

articles.excerpt: The Etosha Pan in northern Namibia, the largest salt flat in the country, looks otherworldly in this satellite photo.
articles.body: The Etosha Pan, Namibia's largest salt pan, seen from space. (Image credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) A neon blue pool swirls amongst what look like clouds, all surrounded by a bright red stretch of land. This might look like the surface of an alien planet , but it's actually a salt flat right here on Earth , seen from space. What is it? Etosha National Park in northern Namibia hosts the largest salt pan, or piece of land covered with salt and other minerals, in the country. This image of the Etosha Pan was captured on April 5 of this year by Europe's Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission, which consists of two identical satellites in the same orbit.
